paper.title: Sequential Transfer in Multi-armed Bandit with Finite Set of Models

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-armed bandit with finite (known) set of models
unmapped: The learner knows a finite set Theta of m candidate models (mean vectors) containing the true model; the number of models m_mod is known
settings.definition_quote: We focus on the setting where there exists a set of models $\Theta = \{\theta = (\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_K)\}$, $|\Theta|=m$, which contains all the possible bandit problems. ... The \textit{mUCB} (model-UCB) algorithm in Fig.~\ref{f:mucb} takes as input a set of models $\Theta$ including the current (unknown) model $\btheta$.

settings.name_in_paper: Sequential transfer in MAB (tasks drawn from distribution rho over an unknown finite set of models)
unmapped: Multi-task / sequential transfer: J episodes of n steps; at each episode a latent task (model) is drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution rho over an unknown finite set of m models and is not revealed; regret is summed over episodes against each episode's optimal arm
The learner knows the number of models m_mod and the number of episodes J_ep
Model means assumed linearly independent and rho(theta) > 0 (Assumption 1)
settings.definition_quote: We consider the sequential transfer setting where at each episode $j$ the learner interacts with a task $\btheta^j$, drawn from a distribution $\rho$ over $\Theta$, for $n$ steps. The objective is to minimize the (pseudo-)regret over $J$ episodes ... The only information available to the learner is the number of models $m$, number of episodes $J$ and number of steps $n$ per task.

algorithms.name: RTP (robust tensor power method for model estimation)

symbols.sum_Aplus: sum over arms in A_+, arms optimal for at least one optimistic model (mu_*(theta) >= mu_*(true model))
symbols.Gamma_i: min over optimistic models theta with optimal arm i of the model gap |mu_i(theta) - mu_i(true theta)|

conditions: the true model belongs to the known set Theta of m models

source.label: thm:mucb.regret
source.quote: If \textit{mUCB} is run with $\delta=1/n$, a set of $m$ models $\Theta$ such that the $\btheta\in\Theta$ and ... then its expected regret is \E[\R_n] \leq K +\sum_{i\in \A_+} \frac{2\Delta_i(\btheta)\log (mn^3)}{\min_{\theta\in\Theta_{+,i}}\Gamma_i(\theta,\btheta)^2} \leq K +\sum_{i\in \A_+} \frac{2\log (m n^3)}{\min_{\theta\in\Theta_{+,i}}\Gamma_i(\theta,\btheta)}

results.notes: Regret defined via pull counts times gaps (pseudo-regret). Reward range not stated explicitly; Hoeffding with 2exp(-2T eps^2) implies [0,1].

source.label: thm:final.bound
source.quote: If \textit{tUCB} is run over $J$ episodes of $n$ steps in which the tasks $\btheta^j$ are drawn from a fixed distribution $\rho$ over a set of models $\Theta$, then its cumulative regret is \R_J \leq JK + ... w.p. $1-\delta$ w.r.t. the randomization over tasks and the realizations of the arms in each episode.

results.notes: Cumulative pseudo-regret (pull counts times gaps) holding w.p. 1-delta. T denotes per-episode length n.
